Ghostty shell integration on Omarchy

Ghostty's shell scripts without the terminal — prompt marks, title tracking, and opt-in sudo/ssh wrappers.

Reviewed 2026-11-04 · independent editorial guide

Short answer

Install with omarchy pkg add ghostty-shell-integration for the bash/zsh/fish/elvish/nushell integration scripts without installing Ghostty itself. Inside Ghostty they're auto-injected; this split package exists for other terminals, shared dotfiles, and machines that only need the sudo/ssh wrapper extras. Verify with echo $GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR. If you already run Ghostty, you already have these scripts.

Ghostty Shell Integration on Omarchy

Ghostty's shell-integration scripts (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, nushell) as a standalone package — semantic prompt marks, working-directory tracking, cursor/title handling, and opt-in sudo/ssh wrappers — without installing the Ghostty terminal itself.

TL;DR

omarchy pkg add ghostty-shell-integration
# inside Ghostty, verify injection happened:
echo $GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR

If you already run Ghostty, you likely have these scripts already — the full Ghostty package bundles them (distro specs list them as dependencies of the main package). This split package exists for machines and setups that want the scripts without the GUI: a different terminal plus Ghostty's ssh/sudo automation, or dotfiles synced across machines where only some run Ghostty.

Getting started (5 minutes)

1. Install, then let Ghostty inject it.

Ghostty auto-injects the integration for the initially launched shell of a supported shell — no rc-file edits needed in most cases. Supported shells: bash, zsh, fish, elvish, nushell, detected by basename match (force one with shell-integration = fish in ~/.config/ghostty/config; disable entirely with shell-integration = none).

2. The three things everyone needs to know:

  • Verify it's actually loaded. Check Ghostty's log for shell integration automatically injected shell=termio.shell_integration.Shell.zsh (or your shell), or functionally: jump-to-prompt keybinds work, the window title tracks your command, and Ghostty doesn't ask to confirm closing when you're sitting at a fresh prompt. If the env var GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR is empty, injection didn't happen — see the manual sourcing fix below.
  • Manual sourcing for the edge cases. Auto-injection only applies to the initially launched shell. If you switch shells inside Ghostty (bash, fish, nix-shell), source the script yourself — bash goes at the top of ~/.bashrc: 
    if [ -n "${GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR}" ]; then
    builtin source "${GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR}/shell-integration/bash/ghostty.bash"
fi
    zsh: ${GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR}/shell-integration/zsh/ghostty-integration; fish: "$GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR"/shell-integration/fish/vendor_conf.d/ghostty-shell-integration.fish. (Per-shell paths from the docs.)
  • The opt-in extras are the real prize. In ~/.config/ghostty/config: 
    shell-integration-features = sudo            # wrap sudo to preserve TERMINFO
shell-integration-features = ssh-env,ssh-terminfo   # wrap ssh for remote setup
    The sudo wrapper fixes sudo htop breaking under TERM=xterm-ghostty; the ssh wrappers auto-install Ghostty's terminfo on first connect (see the ghostty-terminfo guide). They're off by default — upstream chose default-off after debate; mitchellh landed the sudo feature in PR #1294. Note the ssh wrapper is a shell function, so it doesn't apply to scripts, mosh, rsync -e ssh, git, scp, or non-interactive shells — for those, use ghostty +ssh (1.4+) directly or set it in ~/.ssh/config.

3. Fish 4.0+ users get a discount.

Fish 4.0+ has built-in prompt marking, so jump_to_prompt, prompt resizing, and prompt selection work without the integration at all. You'd still install this for the Ghostty-specific extras (sudo/ssh wrappers). (Per the docs.)

Common issues & fixes

sudo htop (or any sudo'd TUI) errors under Ghostty with an unknown-terminal complaint

Fix: sudo strips TERMINFO — and sudo -E alone doesn't help, since /etc/sudoers must also permit the variable (mitchellh's note). Enable the integration's sudo wrapper: shell-integration-features = sudo in your Ghostty config. Real issue: ghostty-org/ghostty#1291. Unverified: whether Omarchy's default sudoers config interferes with the wrapper — on the verify list.

No shell integration at all — prompts behave plainly, no jump-to-prompt

Fix: The documented culprit is GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR not pointing at the resources dir (Ghostty built/installed in a non-standard FHS layout). The log will show shell could not be detected, no automatic shell integration will be injected or ghostty terminfo not found, using xterm-256color. Set GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR manually — but treat it as a red flag that something else is wrong with the install and investigate. (Docs.)

Integration works, then vanishes when you bash/fish/nix-shell inside Ghostty

Fix: Expected — automatic injection only applies to the initially launched shell. Manually source the per-shell script in the new shell (paths in "Getting started"). (Docs.)

ssh-env/ssh-terminfo seem to do nothing

Fix: The wrapper is a shell function, not inherited by child processes. It silently skips mosh, gcloud/aws ssh wrappers, scp/sftp, scripts, Makefiles, and cron. Invoke ghostty +ssh -- user@host directly, or put SetEnv TERM=xterm-256color / SendEnv in ~/.ssh/config (OpenSSH 8.7+; the remote needs AcceptEnv for env forwarding). (SSH docs.)

macOS /bin/bash gets no integration even with everything installed

Fix: macOS's bash is 3.2 — too old for automatic integration. Manually source ghostty.bash, or install a modern bash via Homebrew and set it as your login shell. (Docs.) Linux-only readers can ignore this one, but it documents why "install and forget" has limits.

Pairs well with / If you hate this, try

Pairs well with

  • ghostty-terminfo (Omarchy App Store — the other half of the split; install it on servers so the ssh-terminfo automation has somewhere sane to land), ghostty (Omarchy App Store — bundles both scripts and the terminfo; skip the split packages if you run it), and tmux (integration + tmux over SSH is the combo most likely to hit TERM edge cases).

If you hate this, try

  • nothing — shell integration is optional by design (shell-integration = none in Ghostty config turns it all off). If you only miss one feature, check whether your shell does it natively first (fish 4.0+ covers prompt marking on its own).

Frequently asked questions

Do I need this if I already use Ghostty?

No — the full Ghostty package ships the integration scripts (distro specs declare them as subpackage dependencies of the main package, e.g. Terra's ghostty.spec). This package is for setups that want the scripts without the terminal.

Which shells are supported?

bash, zsh, fish, elvish, nushell — auto-injected by basename match. Force one with shell-integration = <shell>; disable with shell-integration = none. (Docs.)

How do I verify it's working?

Check Ghostty's log for shell integration automatically injected shell=...; functionally, window-title tracking, prompt-keybind scrolling, and no-close-confirm at a prompt confirm it.

Why is the sudo wrapper off by default?

Upstream debated it — kitty aliases sudo by default, but some Ghostty contributors argued a shell shouldn't alias sudo. mitchellh landed shell-integration-features = sudo default-off in PR #1294. (Issue #1291.)

Does the ssh wrapper work with mosh or scp?

No — it's a shell function, invisible to child processes and non-interactive shells. Use ghostty +ssh (1.4+) directly or ~/.ssh/config for those cases. (SSH docs.)
